clues.text: This person’s Ph.D. dissertation, about the importance of individual religious experiences, is called The Concept of the Guardian Spirit in North America.
This author discussed a quarrel between the Uretsiti and the Naotsiti in the book Tales of the Cochiti Indians.
This anthropologist used the studies by Reo Fortune of the Dobu Tribe, identifying them as "treacherous" in a work that also studied the Kwakiutl and Zuni.
In one pamphlet, this thinker denounced the racism of "green devils" using examples from cartoons.

This thinker called cultures “personality writ large” in a work which compared the Dobu, Kwakiutl, and Zuni Cultures.

Along with Gene Weltfish, this anthropologist wrote a pamphlet which refuted biometric head measuring as a means of determining intelligence, insisting that every race had equal potential for intelligence.

This thinker briefly gave now-lost lectures near Philadelphia describing a “low synergy” society as one where the interest of an individual and a society are at odds, a concept developed through observation of cultures.
In one introduction, this colleague of Gene Weltfish stated that "the goal is a world made safe for differences."
This thinker contrasted the emphasis on restraint in cultures of the American Southwest with the focus on abandon in the Great Plains.
She wrote about an “arc of culture,” and compared the Pueblo peoples and Great Plains people’s cultures of restraint and abandon.

In one of this anthropologist’s best known works, this student of Franz Boas and author of “The Races of Mankind” studied newspaper clippings and classic novels and compared “guilt” and “shame” cultures, writing about rituals like seppuku, while she also wrote a book which defined its title concept as the shared beliefs and experiences of a people.
During World War II, she worked for the Office of War Information and derived her most famous work from an assignment to do a study on Japanese culture.
This thinker used newspaper clippings to conduct “anthropology at a distance” and write a book that contrasts the shame and guilt cultures of two different countries.
A later work contrasted guilt and shame cultures and was written despite her lack of firsthand experience with the society in question.
